title: Senators Demand to Know if Dr. Oz Collaborated With Election Denial Groups
gist: Democratic senators led by Elizabeth Warren demand CMS head Mehmet Oz disclose communications with election-denial groups after a July 2026 memo rescinded nursing home voting-assistance guidance and fueled voter-fraud claims.

insights.claim: In July 2026 CMS rescinded guidance on helping nursing home residents vote and replaced it with warnings of prosecution for coercion, after which election-denial groups began alleging fraud in care facilities.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Policy changes can seed conspiracy narratives and harassment of care-facility staff.
insights.locator: In July, Oz's agency issued a memo

insights.claim: Cleta Mitchell's Election Integrity Network led the campaign, claiming left-wing groups steal votes from vulnerable nursing home residents.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Election-denial groups are using agency actions as evidence for narratives.
insights.locator: These left-wing groups go into the nursing homes

insights.claim: Senators including Warren, Blumenthal, Padilla and Booker asked CMS to rescind the memo, reinstate its 2020 and 2024 guidance, and identify communications with Mitchell, EIN and Project Civica.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Possible oversight follow-up if Democrats win a chamber.

insights.claim: Project Civica says it had no communications with CMS about the memo or its Adopt a Care Facility initiative.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.locator: We have had no communications or interactions with CMS

insights.claim: Oz wrote in September that neutral logistical help like requesting a ballot or arranging transportation would not trigger a fraud investigation, yet CMS has not reinstated the prior guidance.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Mixed signals create legal uncertainty for nursing home operators.
